A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same topological MIL framework and retain matching core experiments despite renaming and reorganization. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original toy, synthetic MIL, benchmark, and anemia-classification experiments, including repeated-run results and instance-level analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and additionally reports sensitivity experiments, higher-order topology ablations, a shortcut-learning test, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: TR-MIL becomes TG-MIL, but the encoder/pooling framework and combined classification and bidirectional topological loss remain unchanged (Equations 2–5). Higher-dimensional experiments exercise support for arbitrary homology dimensions already stated in v2.

E1.justification: v3 adds a targeted Gaussian-concept unit-test scenario with reversed training/test bait correlations (Section 5.4). The hypersphere toy data, MNIST/FashionMNIST bags, five classic MIL benchmarks, and anemia cohort remain.

E2.justification: Compared with v2 Table 1, v3 Table 2 adds GNNMIL, DistNet, APMILwD, and GAPMILwD while retaining previous comparators. These added comparison scores come from cited papers; RGMIL remains the explicitly reimplemented benchmark comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation configurations using higher homology dimensions, five-value topological-loss coefficient sweeps, a bait-correlation reversal protocol with AUC and balanced accuracy, and runtime measurements at specified bag sizes. Existing synthetic bag configurations, benchmark cross-validation, and patient-based anemia splits are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test homology order (Table 2), coefficient sensitivity (Figures 4–5 and Tables 8, 10), shortcut susceptibility, and computational scaling (Sections 5.4–5.5). Appendix Figure 9 expands the earlier training-curve analysis with separate classification and topological loss curves.

E5.justification: Beyond v2's means and standard deviations, v3 introduces Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and Bonferroni correction for 24 comparisons per synthetic dataset, reporting p-values in Table 1. This adds inferential statistical reporting without establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds higher-order topology, sensitivity, significance, unit-test, and timing results. Anomaly-aware anemia accuracy changes from 79.50 ± 1.2 to 81.1 ± 2.2, and F1 from 77.01 ± 1.8 to 79.2 ± 2.6 (v2 Table 2; v3 Table 3). Original 0D benchmark scores are unchanged after percentage conversion, but added dropout baselines surpass them on MUSK1 and FOX.

T1.justification: v3 adds a monotone bag-label assumption, bag/instance-risk definitions, and an instance-learnability argument (Equations 6–10), plus a permutation-invariance argument assuming unique pairwise distances. Equation 1 also substantively changes from an all-pairs simplex condition to an existential-neighbor expression; this is not equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The principal performance and generalization claims, including the abstract's 15.3%, 2.8%, and 5.5% improvements, remain. v3 narrows novelty from the first method improving scarce-data MIL generalizability to the first topological method, and explicitly emphasizes end-to-end training.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies anomaly-score consistency as representation evidence rather than instance-level diagnostic reliability. It adds limitations concerning visually complex or noisy images, discusses feature-level topology as an alternative, interprets higher-order topology results, and reports pooling-dependent shortcut-test behavior. These substantially refine applicability and failure conditions.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a public code-repository address and explains that anemia data require a request to their owners. It additionally documents cell-image zero-padding, coefficient-selection guidance, A100 hardware, 228 hours of experiments, and measured computational costs; most existing architecture tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around frozen-encoder histopathology methods versus end-to-end instance learning, including reasons for excluding certain comparisons. v3 adds recent MIL methods, Deep Sets/PointNet positioning, instance-learnability research, and algorithmic unit-test literature, while narrowing its novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Synthetic experiments precede benchmarks in v3, appendices are reorganized by experiment family, and the title and TR-MIL terminology change throughout.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a single-column journal format, redraws the framework diagram, and rearranges existing plots. It adds sensitivity plots and statistical/unit-test tables, expands the benchmark table, and moves and enlarges the synthetic learning-curve figure with additional loss panels.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 makes the retained method easier to assess through sensitivity controls, updated comparisons, measured overhead, access information, and clearer applicability limits. These gains are tempered by reduced mathematical precision in Equation 1 and inconsistent new reporting: Table 1 marks six significant cases while the text claims seven, and the unit-test failure label at AUC 0.50 does not follow the stated strict below-0.5 criterion. The net improvement is positive but limited.
